findings.title: enableSqlExpressions has inverted, dead logic and always returns false
findings.body: The new enableSqlExpressions helper computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` — so `enabled` is true when the flag is DISABLED — then returns false in both branches, making the function unconditionally false and the flag check pointless. The variable name/logic is inverted and misleading. Consequence: the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle now has no effect at all, and any future maintainer who 'fixes' the obvious inversion (returning `enabled`) would re-enable the vulnerable code path. The function should either be deleted entirely (the stub DB already blocks execution) or written to explicitly and permanently return false with a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264.

findings.title: Error message "sqlExpressions is not implemented" is wrong and misleading
findings.body: When a user submits a SQL expression query, they get `sqlExpressions is not implemented`. The feature was implemented and then deliberately disabled for security reasons (CVE-2024-9264). The message misleads users into thinking it's a temporary gap, and doesn't mention the feature flag. A message like "SQL expressions have been disabled" (ideally referencing the flag/CVE) would be accurate and actionable.

findings.title: Legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path is not gated by the new reader check
findings.body: The feature-flag/disabled check was only added to the new `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` path (reader.go), but `UnmarshalSQLCommand` (used for the legacy/rawNode query format) still constructs and executes `SQLCommand` without any check. Execution is only prevented because the stub DB in pkg/expr/sql/db.go always returns "not implemented". This means the disable logic is inconsistent across entry points, and if the stub DB is ever re-implemented (or the enableSqlExpressions inversion fixed), the legacy path would silently re-enable the vulnerable feature. The guard should live in NewSQLCommand (or both paths) so all construction sites are covered.

findings.title: Stub DB returns generic "not implemented" errors that surface as confusing 400s
findings.body: All DB methods return `errors.New("not implemented")`. Via NewSQLCommand -> sql.TablesList, a user query now fails with a generic BadRequest "error reading SQL command" (or a raw "not implemented" from Execute) with no indication that SQL expressions were intentionally disabled. Since these stubs exist purely to neutralize the DuckDB dependency, the errors should state that SQL expressions are disabled so users and support can diagnose it.

findings.title: TablesList is now unreachable dead code with SQL-string building logic retained
findings.body: TablesList builds a DuckDB command via fmt.Sprintf with escaped quotes and calls RunCommands, which now always returns "not implemented", so TablesList can never succeed. Keeping the string-interpolation code that talks to a (removed) DuckDB API is dead weight and a hazard if someone wires a real implementation back in (the naive quote-escaping was part of the injection surface). Either delete parser.go's command-building path along with the dependency, or leave a clear comment that this is intentionally disabled.

findings.title: No tests added or updated for the disabled SQL expression behavior
findings.body: This PR removes a whole feature (SQL expressions) and changes the behavior of the QueryTypeSQL path, but includes no test changes: there is no test asserting that SQL expression queries now return an error regardless of the feature toggle, no test covering the legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path, and any existing tests of sql expressions (e.g. around sql_command.go / sql parser) appear untouched and will either fail or silently no longer exercise the real behavior. A regression test pinning the 'always disabled' behavior would prevent someone from accidentally re-enabling it.
